Question_text: BKH is a large public limited company. It has 2000 employees across 18 locations. BKH sells a range of insurance products including house and car insurance. BKH's shareholders want the business to increase profit. The Managing Director knows increasing profit can conflict with the objectives of other stakeholder groups. She said: 'Private sector businesses have different objectives to public sector organisations.' BKH is also planning to expand by taking over another insurance company.
Sub_topic: Classify private sector, public sector in mixed economy
Different objectives: survival, growth, profit, market share
Methods of measuring size: employees, output, capital employed
Concept of economies of scale, examples: purchasing, marketing, financial, managerial, technical

Question_text: Alex started APB as a sole trader business 4 years ago. APB provide printing services for local businesses such as leaflets and brochures. Alex thinks having a good location is important to any business. All APB's 6 employees receive on-the-job training. Alex has a democratic leadership style and uses job rotation to help keep employees motivated. To meet an increase in demand, Alex plans to buy an additional printing machine. This will cost $1800. Alex has to decide on an appropriate source of finance.
Sub_topic: Non-financial: job enrichment, rotation, teamworking, training, promotion
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Features of leadership: autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire
Factors in choice: size, legal form, amount, time, loans
